hypothesis: Replacing the current class-weight treatment with a class-frequency-calibrated focal loss (inverse-frequency alpha and gamma=2.0) will upweight low-support hazardous/precipitation classes and hard examples, improving hazard_class_f1 and overall macro_f1 without materially harming forecast RMSE.
evidence_anchor: Hazard class F1 fluctuates from 0.53 to 0.79 across seeds; ZBAA hazard support is only 94 and ZSPD/ZSSS val labels are near single-class; baseline scratch classification_macro_f1 is only 0.750 vs pretrained 0.804.
expected_effect: classification_macro_f1 improves by >0.005; hazard_class_f1 stabilizes or increases; forecast RMSE remains approximately unchanged.
falsification: If paired classification_macro_f1 improvement versus parent is <0.0005, or hazard_class_f1 decreases, the trial is refuted.
patch_plan: In compute_class_weights, form class alpha from train_label_counts using inverse_freq. In classification_loss, implement focal loss as -alpha_c * (1 - p_c)^gamma * log(p_c) with gamma=2.0 and the passed class_weights, while preserving signature and guarding masked/virtual runway cases.
